payload.prompt:
I need two Solidity smart contracts that work together for an INR-backed token and a Uniswap v4 hook for UPI withdrawals.
Indian Rupee Token (INRT)
It’s an ERC-20 token named “Indian Rupee Token” with symbol “INRT”.
It represents rupees backed 1:1 by real bank deposits.
Only the owner can mint tokens after confirming a bank deposit, and each mint is tied to a unique bankTxIdso the same deposit can’t be counted twice.
When users withdraw to a UPI bank account, tokens must be burned.
The burn can be triggered either by the owner or by a separate Hook contract that we’ll build.
Keep a running total of the real INR reserves in totalBankReserves.
Increase reserves on mint, decrease on burn.
Track every withdrawal request in a struct containing the user’s address, amount, UPI ID, timestamp, and a processed flag.
Emit events whenever tokens are minted, burned, or a withdrawal is requested, so the backend can listen to them.
Include pausable transfers for emergencies.
Owner should be able to pause/unpause, authorize or revoke the hook contract, and mark a withdrawal as processed after the INR is actually paid out.
Add view functions to check a withdrawal’s details, whether a bankTxId has been processed, and a backing-ratio view that reports totalBankReserves ÷ totalSupply.
CryptoUPIHook
This is a Uniswap v4 BaseHook contract.
It is attached to the USDT/INRT liquidity pool.
Whenever someone swaps USDT → INRT and passes extra hook-data with a requestId and their upiId, the hook should:
Decode those two fields.
Check the request hasn’t already been handled.
Work out how many INRT tokens were received in the swap.
Emit a WithdrawalRequested event including requestId, user address, amount of INRT, and their UPI ID.
The hook itself doesn’t transfer or burn tokens during the swap — it just logs the intent.
Later, an owner-only function processWithdrawal() lets the operator call into the INRT contract’s burnForWithdrawal() to actually burn the INRT tokens for that user.
Track which requestIds have already been processed to avoid duplicates.
Include a helper to ABI-encode the (requestId, upiId) pair for clients.
Expose a small view to return whether the pool is initialised, which token is USDT, and the poolId.
Common details for both contracts
SPDX license should be MIT.
Use Solidity ^0.8.26.
Use OpenZeppelin v5 for ERC20, Ownable, and Pausable.
Keep the code clear, well-commented, and follow good require-message and event-naming practice.
Don’t add any features that aren’t described above.
